hypothesis: A different text-to-mel architecture with explicit stop prediction may provide complete short wake/near-word and command source waveforms without the duration failures observed in both Parler decoding protocols. Only source feasibility is tested; any training incorporation needs its own fixed experiment.
role_decision: CMU ARCTIC speakers appear in existing Piper multispeaker training plan. All seven are training-only, never independent development or acceptance. Historical use does not establish this new waveform byte identity; it does establish known speaker-family overlap. Pretraining overlap remains unknown.
history_evidence: 4090-multispeaker-coverage-native-plan-v1.json, en_US-arctic-medium speaker_id_map and training requests; no claim this plan alone proves every historical request executed.
speed: Engine native rate only; no exposed speaking-rate control authenticated. Any future complete-waveform speed/noise/RIR augmentation requires a separate frozen manifest.
metadata: Text tokenizer IDs and decoder stop logits are available, not generated phonemes/durations. No phonetic correctness or speaker generalization claim.
required: Completed weights, zip and actual package hashes, generator and upstream implementation hash in pushed execution lock before run.
